A 68-year-old man is evaluated in the emergency department for 2 weeks of constipation, polyuria, and confusion. He has a 50 pack-year smoking history and has lost 6 kg over 3 months. Vital signs: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, pulse 96/min, mild dry mucous membranes. Serum calcium is 13.2 mg/dL, albumin 3.8 g/dL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL, and phosphate 2.1 mg/dL. Chest CT shows a 5 cm central cavitating mass with hilar adenopathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next test to establish the mechanism of hypercalcemia?

A 52-year-old man who smokes 1.5 packs daily presents to the clinic with four months of weight loss, proximal muscle weakness, and new purple abdominal striae. Blood pressure is 168/98 mm Hg and he has new glucose intolerance. Serum potassium is 2.6 mEq/L and bicarbonate is 33 mEq/L. Plasma ACTH is 210 pg/mL and midnight cortisol is 62 mcg/dL. Low-dose and high-dose dexamethasone suppression fail. Chest CT shows a 2-cm right hilar mass. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 52-year-old man with alcohol use disorder is admitted to the hospital with a 4-day history of diarrhea, muscle cramps, and carpopedal spasm despite oral calcium supplementation. Vital signs: temperature 37.1 C, pulse 104/min, blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg. Serum calcium is 7.1 mg/dL, albumin 2.9 g/dL, and potassium 3.0 mEq/L. Serum magnesium is 0.9 mg/dL (normal 1.7-2.2) and PTH is inappropriately low. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 67-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer is seen in the oncology clinic. She reports progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided pleuritic discomfort. This is her third thoracentesis in 5 weeks, each removing about 1.5 liters with rapid reaccumulation. Pleural fluid cytology shows adenocarcinoma cells. Chest CT shows a moderate right effusion with a thickened visceral pleura and a lung that does not re-expand. Her performance status is ECOG 2. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 71-year-old man in an outpatient nephrology clinic has worsening kidney function three weeks after starting lisinopril for hypertension. He has peripheral artery disease and a 60-pack-year smoking history. Blood pressure is 150/88 mm Hg, and abdominal examination reveals bruits over both flanks. Serum creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 2.0 mg/dL, and potassium is 5.4 mEq/L. Urinalysis shows no protein or cells, and renal ultrasound shows kidneys of similar size. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 68-year-old man in a cardiology follow-up clinic returns three weeks after coronary angiography through a femoral artery. He reports fatigue, weight loss, and new pain in both feet. Blood pressure is 158/92 mm Hg. Examination shows mottled livedo reticularis on both legs and two dusky toes with patchy blue discoloration. Creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 2.1 mg/dL, eosinophils are 14 percent, and urinalysis shows mild proteinuria without red cells. He takes aspirin and atorvastatin. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the emergency department 6 days after oocyte retrieval for in vitro fertilization. She has abdominal bloating, nausea and a 3-kg weight gain over 3 days, with reduced urine output. Blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg, pulse 112/min, temperature 37.0 C. The abdomen is distended and tender with shifting dullness. Hematocrit is 52 percent, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL and serum albumin 2.8 g/dL. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 10-year-old boy who had a Kasai portoenterostomy for biliary atresia at 2 months of age is brought to the emergency department in Boston after vomiting about 300 mL of bright red blood. He is pale and tachycardic, with pulse 128/min and blood pressure 84/50 mm Hg. Examination shows splenomegaly and ascites. Labs: hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, platelet count 92,000/mm3, INR 1.4, total bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL. He has already received 2 liters of crystalloid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacologic intervention now?

A 13-year-old boy is admitted to the pediatric unit with ascending weakness that began in his legs 6 days ago. Three weeks earlier he had watery diarrhea. Examination shows absent knee and ankle reflexes and symmetric arm weakness without a sensory level. Blood pressure is 142/88 mm Hg, heart rate 118/min, and respiratory rate 24/min. Forced vital capacity is 1.1 L, and the predicted value is 2.6 L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 16-year-old girl is brought to the adolescent clinic by her mother for progressive weight loss over 8 months. She restricts intake to under 800 calories daily, exercises for two hours after school, and has not had a menstrual period in 6 months. Height 1.65 m, weight 36 kg, BMI 13.2. Temperature 35.8 C, pulse 38/min, blood pressure 84/50 mm Hg supine and 72/40 mm Hg standing. Her potassium is 3.2 mmol/L. She has no suicidal ideation. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 67-year-old man with bipolar disorder presents to the emergency department with 2 days of vomiting, coarse hand tremor, and unsteady gait. He takes lithium carbonate, and 3 days ago he started naproxen for knee pain. He is alert and oriented. Temperature is 37.2 degrees C, pulse 98/min, and blood pressure 102/64 mm Hg. Serum lithium level is 2.2 mEq/L, and creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 2.1 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 19-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa is admitted to the medical unit after 4 weeks of minimal oral intake and a 9 kg weight loss. Her BMI is 14.2 kg/m2. She is lethargic, and cardiac examination shows bradycardia to 48/min with orthostatic hypotension. Serum potassium is 3.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.4 mg/dL, and phosphate 2.0 mg/dL. Nutritional support via nasogastric tube is planned. What is the most appropriate next step before starting feeds?

A 41-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder presents to the emergency department with three days of vomiting, diarrhea, coarse hand tremor, and unsteadiness. Hydrochlorothiazide was started for hypertension last week. She takes lithium carbonate 900 mg nightly. She is drowsy but oriented. Heart rate is 102/min and blood pressure 118/74 mm Hg. Serum creatinine is 1.9 mg/dL, up from 0.9, and lithium is 2.1 mEq/L. What is the best next step?

A 52-year-old man presents to the transplant clinic 3 weeks after deceased-donor kidney transplantation with right leg swelling and groin fullness. He has no fever, dysuria, or wound drainage. Blood pressure is 142/88 mm Hg and temperature 36.9 C. Serum creatinine has risen from 1.4 to 2.6 mg/dL over one week. Ultrasound shows a 9 cm, anechoic, well-defined collection anterior to the graft with new hydronephrosis of the graft. Urine output is preserved. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 27-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa is admitted to a medical ward with a weight of 38 kg and BMI 13.5 after 2 weeks of almost no oral intake. Dextrose-containing intravenous fluids were started on admission, and enteral feeding began this morning. Today she is confused, has a heart rate of 118/min, and has mild leg weakness. Serum phosphorus is 1.1 mg/dL, potassium 2.9 mEq/L, and magnesium 1.2 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis presents to the hepatology clinic for routine follow-up. He has no history of hematemesis, melena or encephalopathy and takes no medications except a multivitamin. He has been abstinent from alcohol for 2 years. Vital signs: blood pressure 118/72 mm Hg, pulse 78/min. Platelets 96,000/mm3, total bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, albumin 3.6 g/dL, INR 1.2. Upper endoscopy last month shows medium-caliber esophageal varices without red wale marks. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 42-year-old woman presents to the transplant clinic 4 days after receiving a deceased-donor kidney transplant with fever, a tender graft and decreased urine output. Her temperature is 38.1 C and blood pressure is 150/92 mmHg. Serum creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 2.6 mg/dL. Renal Doppler ultrasound shows normal arterial and venous flow, and urinalysis shows no evidence of infection. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man is seen in the transplant clinic on postoperative day 12 after deceased-donor kidney transplantation. He reports reduced urine output and mild flank tenderness over the graft. He is afebrile, with blood pressure 142/88 mm Hg. Serum creatinine has risen from 1.2 mg/dL at discharge to 2.6 mg/dL. Tacrolimus trough is within target. Urinalysis shows no red cells or casts. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 61-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes is admitted from the emergency department with right flank pain, fever, and rigors. She has vomited twice and her urine output has fallen over the past 12 hours. Temperature is 39.4 C, blood pressure 92/58 mm Hg, and heart rate 118/min. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites. Creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 2.6 mg/dL. Noncontrast CT shows a 9 mm obstructing right ureteral stone with perinephric stranding and right hydronephrosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

Consider the following statements about the arterial circle of Willis and its branches: 1. The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid and posterior cerebral arteries. 2. The anterior communicating artery connects the two anterior cerebral arteries. 3. The lenticulostriate arteries arise from the anterior cerebral artery. 4. The basilar artery gives off the anterior spinal artery. Which statements are correct?

A 45-year-old woman has a sudden thunderclap headache, and angiography shows a berry aneurysm at a common site. Consider the following statements about the circle of Willis: 1. The anterior communicating artery joins the two anterior cerebral arteries. 2. The posterior communicating artery joins the internal carotid and posterior cerebral arteries. 3. The basilar artery bifurcates into the two posterior cerebral arteries. 4. The middle cerebral artery forms part of the circle. Which statements are correct?

A 70-year-old woman falls and has a displaced intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck. Which statements explain the risk of avascular necrosis of the femoral head? 1. The retinacular vessels run along the neck beneath the synovial reflection. 2. The medial circumflex femoral artery is the main contributor. 3. The artery of the ligament of the head provides most of the adult supply. 4. The nutrient artery of the femoral shaft supplies the head in adults. Which combination is correct?

A 40-year-old man is being assessed for hip stability. Consider these statements: 1. Iliofemoral ligament prevents hyperextension. 2. Ligament of head of femur is the main stabiliser in adults. 3. Hip capsule attaches anteriorly to the intertrochanteric line. 4. Pubofemoral ligament limits excessive abduction. Which combination is correct?

A 55-year-old man undergoes coronary angiography. Consider these statements about the coronary circulation: 1. The great cardiac vein accompanies the anterior interventricular artery. 2. The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium. 3. The middle cardiac vein runs in the posterior interventricular groove. 4. The anterior cardiac veins drain into the coronary sinus. Which statements are correct?

A 66-year-old woman has a posterior wall infarct. Angiography shows a right-dominant circulation. Consider these statements: 1. The posterior interventricular artery arises from the right coronary artery. 2. The coronary sinus drains into the right atrium. 3. The great cardiac vein accompanies the posterior interventricular artery. 4. The anterior interventricular artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the septum. Which statements are correct?

Consider the following statements about the knee joint and popliteal fossa: 1. Popliteus unlocks the fully extended knee by laterally rotating the femur on the fixed tibia. 2. The medial meniscus is firmly attached to the tibial collateral ligament. 3. The popliteal artery is the most superficial structure in the fossa. 4. The lateral meniscus is more commonly injured than the medial. Which statements are correct?

A 30-year-old woman has a medial knee injury after a twisting fall. The unhappy triad is suspected. Which combination of structures is injured? 1. Anterior cruciate ligament 2. Tibial collateral ligament 3. Medial meniscus 4. Lateral meniscus Which is correct?

A 30-year-old man has weakness after a viral illness. Nerve conduction studies show markedly slowed conduction with preserved axons. Which statements about myelination are correct? 1. Schwann cells myelinate a single internode of one peripheral axon 2. One oligodendrocyte can myelinate several central axons 3. Nodes of Ranvier are sites of saltatory conduction 4. Peripheral myelin is formed by astrocytes

A 30-year-old woman has a demyelinating disorder affecting only the central nervous system, with sparing of peripheral nerves. Which statement about myelination correctly explains the cell-level differences? 1. One oligodendrocyte myelinates several CNS axon segments 2. One Schwann cell myelinates one internode of a single axon 3. Schwann cells can regenerate-support injured axons 4. Oligodendrocytes have a basal lamina

Consider these statements about the scalp: 1. The loose areolar layer is the site where scalp infections spread widely. 2. Scalp hemorrhage is profuse partly because vessels are held open by dense connective tissue. 3. Lymph from the occipital region drains first to the submandibular nodes. 4. The epicranial aponeurosis connects frontalis and occipitalis. Which statements are correct?

A 25-year-old footballer sustains an acute hamstring injury during sprinting. Consider these statements about the posterior thigh: 1. Biceps femoris long head arises from the ischial tuberosity. 2. Semitendinosus, semimembranosus and biceps short head are all supplied by the tibial part of sciatic nerve. 3. The hamstring part of adductor magnus extends the hip. 4. Sciatic nerve lies deep to the long head of biceps femoris in the upper thigh. Which statements are correct?

A 60-year-old man has rib fracture and a hematoma in the 6th intercostal space. Consider the neurovascular bundle in this space. Which statements are correct? 1. The vein lies most superior in the costal groove. 2. The collateral branches run along the upper border of the rib below. 3. The bundle lies between the innermost intercostal and internal intercostal muscles. 4. Posterior intercostal arteries of spaces 3 to 11 arise from the thoracic aorta.

A 45-year-old woman with breast carcinoma has axillary surgery. Consider these statements about the thoracic wall: 1. The intercostal nerves T1 to T6 are purely thoracic in distribution 2. The internal thoracic artery gives anterior intercostal arteries to the upper six spaces 3. The posterior intercostal arteries of the lower nine spaces arise from the descending thoracic aorta 4. The intercostal vein lies deepest in the costal groove Which statements are correct?

A 40-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis develops confusion and asterixis after a gastrointestinal bleed. Consider the mechanisms underlying his encephalopathy: 1. Brain astrocytes convert excess ammonia and glutamate to glutamine 2. Glutamine accumulation causes astrocyte swelling 3. Depletion of alpha-ketoglutarate impairs the brain TCA cycle 4. Ammonia increases activity of the hepatic urea cycle enzymes. Which combination is correct?

A 40-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis develops confusion and asterixis after a gastrointestinal bleed. Consider these statements about ammonia handling in the brain: 1. Astrocytes convert ammonia and glutamate to glutamine. 2. Ammonia depletes alpha-ketoglutarate via glutamate dehydrogenase. 3. Glutamine accumulation causes astrocyte swelling. 4. Ammonia is converted to urea within neurons. Which statements are correct?

A 35-year-old woman on combined oral contraceptive pills has migraine with aura. Consider the statements about combined pills: 1. They reduce ovarian cancer risk. 2. They are contraindicated in migraine with aura. 3. They increase endometrial cancer risk. 4. They reduce benign breast disease. Which combination is correct?

A hospital infection control officer audits an autoclave and wants a biological indicator to confirm sterilising conditions were achieved. Consider these statements: 1. Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores are used for autoclaves. 2. Bacillus atrophaeus spores are used for hot air ovens. 3. Chemical indicator tape alone proves sterility. 4. Clostridium tetani spores are the standard for ethylene oxide. Which statements are correct?

It acts by alkylation of nucleic acids and proteins 2. It is effective for heat-labile items 3. Aeration is required after the cycle to remove residual gas 4. It is not effective in the presence of any humidity Which statements are correct?

In a hospital infection control audit, which of the following statements are correct? 1. Standard precautions apply to all patients irrespective of diagnosis 2. Used needles should be recapped before disposal into sharps containers

The patient asks that her diagnosis and test results not be shared with her parents, and the clinic is in a state that allows minors to consent to STI care. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 58-year-old woman is seen in clinic 3 days after an elective cholecystectomy. Her early recovery was normal. Abdominal CT now shows a retained surgical sponge near the liver bed, and she has mild fever and abdominal pain. Vital signs show temperature 38.2 C, heart rate 98 and blood pressure 124/76. Operating room records show a sponge count discrepancy that was never reconciled. The patient asks what happened. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 46-year-old man who is a general surgeon is evaluated in the hospital where he operates after a nurse reports that he smelled of alcohol before a scheduled colectomy. He has slurred speech, a tremor of the outstretched hands, and bloodshot eyes. He insists he is fit to operate and denies drinking. His pulse is 98/min, blood pressure is 142/88 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.9 C. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 16-year-old girl attends a routine primary care visit alone. She reports a new sexual partner and asks for contraception and testing for sexually transmitted infections, requesting that her parents not be told. Temperature is 36.9 C, blood pressure 112/68 mm Hg, and pulse 74/min, with a normal examination. Her mother, who waited in the lobby, now asks the physician about the results. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 16-year-old girl presents to a primary care clinic in Ohio with her mother for a routine well visit. She is sexually active with one partner and asks for chlamydia and gonorrhea testing without her mother being told. She has no abdominal pain, vaginal discharge, or fever. Vital signs are normal, and her mother asks to remain in the room during the discussion. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 68-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit after a large hemorrhagic stroke and is intubated; she is unresponsive to voice with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 4. She never completed an advance directive or named a health care proxy. Her adult daughter visits daily and asks to make decisions, while her adult son in another state wants all treatment continued. Her previously stated values included never wanting to live on machines. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 41-year-old male surgical attending is observed by a nurse before a morning operation. He has slurred speech, smells of alcohol, and has missed two prior case start times this month. He appears drowsy and has tremulous hands. Vital signs show temperature 36.9 C, heart rate 104 and blood pressure 138/88. A colleague asks what to do, and several scheduled cases remain today. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man is hospitalized on a medical ward for pneumonia. Yesterday he received heparin 10,000 units subcutaneously instead of the ordered 5,000 units, confirmed by pharmacy. Today he is alert, with pulse 92/min and blood pressure 128/76 mm Hg. Hemoglobin has fallen from 13.2 to 11.4 g/dL, and there is no bleeding. He asks why his blood count dropped. An event report has not yet been filed. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 71-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. He has no advance directive or appointed health care agent. Blood pressure is 104/60 mm Hg on low-dose norepinephrine. On day 3 he remains unresponsive without purposeful movement, and neurology judges meaningful recovery unlikely. His wife reports he once said he would not want to live on a ventilator if he could not recognize his family. Their adult son insists all treatment continue. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 44-year-old anesthesiologist is observed by a nurse to have slurred speech and a smell of alcohol shortly before a scheduled case. She denies drinking. Pulse is 96/min, blood pressure 138/88 mm Hg, and temperature 36.9 C, with no focal neurologic deficit. Colleagues report she has missed several morning conferences this month and made two recent medication charting errors. The department chair asks how to proceed. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 47-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision with a pelvic fracture. She is alert and decisionally capable. Blood pressure is 82/50 mm Hg, pulse 124/min, and hemoglobin 6.1 g/dL. She has a signed advance directive and states she refuses blood products because of her religious beliefs. Her surgeon asks whether to transfuse now. She reconfirms her refusal. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 16-year-old girl is seen in a clinic with her mother waiting in the lobby. The patient asks for oral contraception and chlamydia testing, reports sexual activity with one partner for 6 months, and denies pelvic pain or fever. Vital signs are normal. Pelvic examination is unremarkable, and urine nucleic acid amplification testing is pending. The patient asks that her mother not be told about these services. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 47-year-old male anesthesiologist is brought to the employee health office after a colleague reports recent late arrivals, a strong smell of alcohol on two shifts, and a discrepancy in controlled-substance logs. He has a fine tremor and slurred speech but denies any substance use. Vital signs show blood pressure 142/90 mm Hg, pulse 104/min, and temperature 37.0 C. Breath alcohol testing is 0.00 percent. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 71-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with prolonged resuscitation. He remains comatose with extensor posturing to pain, a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 4, and EEG shows diffuse suppression. He has no advance directive or health care proxy. His wife requests withdrawal of ventilation, while his adult son insists on continuing all treatment. The intensivist asks how to proceed. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man is admitted to a community hospital after a pharmacy dispensing error. Overnight he received ten times his intended dose of insulin glargine, and his glucose fell to 38 mg/dL. After dextrose, he is alert with blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg and pulse 84/min. The nurse identified the error and reported it internally to pharmacy and risk management. The patient now asks his physician what happened. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 64-year-old woman with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is admitted to the medical intensive care unit with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure and is on noninvasive ventilation. Her limbs are weak, and she communicates reliably by blinking to yes-or-no questions. She states clearly that she does not want intubation or long-term ventilation and asks that the ventilator be stopped, repeating this to a palliative care physician. Her husband objects, saying she cannot speak for herself. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 33-year-old woman is seen in the genetics clinic with her husband after their first child was diagnosed with VACTERL features at birth. The infant had a repaired tracheoesophageal fistula, anal atresia, a ventricular septal defect, and a radial ray defect. Chromosome breakage studies were normal, and a karyotype showed no abnormality. The family has no relevant history, and the mother is now 12 weeks pregnant. Her vital signs and early ultrasound are unremarkable. What is the most appropriate counselling and next step?

A 1-day-old girl is evaluated on the neonatal unit after delivery at 38 weeks. Since her first feed she has choked, frothed copious secretions and drooled, and feeds come back through the nose. Her abdomen is scaphoid. Vital signs: heart rate 168/min, respiratory rate 62/min, SpO2 91% on room air. A nasogastric tube passed to 10 cm stops in the upper chest and cannot enter the stomach. What is the most appropriate immediate next step?

A 31-year-old woman presents to a clinical genetics clinic with her 3-month-old son. He has a right radial ray defect, a hemivertebra on spine radiograph, and an imperforate anus treated surgically. Echocardiogram and renal ultrasound are normal, intelligence is expected to be typical for age, and chromosome breakage testing is normal. Parents ask about the chance of another affected child. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling?

A 5-day-old boy is seen in the neonatal clinic after a diverting colostomy for anal atresia. He has a hemivertebra on spinal radiographs, a ventricular septal defect on echocardiography, and an absent right radius with a missing right thumb. Renal ultrasound shows right renal agenesis. Choanae, eyes and ears are normal, and chromosome breakage studies are normal. Vital signs are stable and he is afebrile. What is the most likely unifying diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy is referred to a genetics clinic by his pediatrician. He had an anorectal malformation repaired in infancy, a vertebral segmentation anomaly on spine radiograph, and a ventricular septal defect repaired in infancy. He has marked global developmental delay and mild facial dysmorphism. Vital signs are normal, and renal ultrasound is normal. Parents ask whether this is simply VACTERL association. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 67-year-old man presents to his clinic for a preventive visit. He smoked two packs per day for 25 years before quitting 16 years ago. He has no cough, hemoptysis, or weight loss. He has stable coronary artery disease. Vital signs are blood pressure 130/76 mm Hg, pulse 70/min, and SpO2 98 percent. Chest examination is clear. He requests a low-dose chest CT for lung cancer screening because of his heavy smoking history. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 56-year-old woman presents to a breast imaging clinic for routine screening follow-up. She has no breast symptoms or personal history of breast cancer, and her sister was diagnosed at age 60. Her mammogram 2 years ago was normal. Today's screening mammogram is negative, and the radiologist reports heterogeneously dense breast tissue. Vital signs are normal and breast examination is unremarkable. She asks whether a breast ultrasound should be added. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 49-year-old man presents to his primary care clinic for a routine visit. He has smoked one pack per day for 30 years and continues to smoke. He reports no cough, hemoptysis, or weight loss, and he has never had chest imaging. His vital signs are normal, and chest examination is unremarkable. He asks whether he should start annual low-dose CT lung screening now. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

A 58-year-old man presents to his primary care clinic for an annual health visit. He has hypertension and no respiratory symptoms. He smoked one pack per day for 35 years and quit 16 years ago. He walks daily and has no cough or hemoptysis. Vital signs: blood pressure 128/78 mm Hg, pulse 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and SpO2 98 percent on room air. Lung examination is clear. He asks whether he should have lung cancer screening. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 78-year-old woman presents to her primary care clinic for an annual examination. She has no breast complaints and has had regular screening mammograms since her forties. Her most recent mammogram, one year ago, was normal. She has no family history of breast cancer and takes alendronate for osteoporosis. Vital signs are normal, and breast examination shows no masses or nipple discharge. She asks whether she should keep getting mammograms. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 78-year-old woman presents to her primary care clinic for a health maintenance visit. She is independent with good functional status, manages type 2 diabetes with metformin, and expects to live many more years. Her last screening mammogram at age 74 was negative. She has no breast symptoms or personal history of breast cancer, and her vital signs and breast examination are normal. She asks whether she should continue screening mammography. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 78-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes presents to her primary care clinic for an annual visit. She is independent in daily activities and takes metformin and lisinopril. She has had regular screening mammograms since age 45, and her last one 2 years ago was normal. She has no breast symptoms. Vital signs: blood pressure 134/80 mm Hg, pulse 74/min, BMI 29 kg/m2. Breast examination shows no masses. She asks whether she should continue mammography. What is the most appropriate response?

A 58-year-old woman presents to a community health clinic to discuss prevention. She has smoked one pack per day for 18 years and currently smokes. She has no cough, hemoptysis, or weight loss. She has no chronic lung disease, and her chest examination is normal. Vital signs show blood pressure 128/78 mm Hg, pulse 80/min, and SpO2 98 percent. She wants a lung scan because her sister had lung cancer. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 63-year-old man with COPD presents to a pulmonary clinic for his annual lung cancer screening visit. He smoked 1.5 packs per day for 40 years and quit 9 years ago. Three months ago he was hospitalized for decompensated heart failure, and echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 20 percent. He uses home oxygen, walks with a walker, and says he would decline lung surgery. Vital signs: blood pressure 110/68 mm Hg, pulse 96/min, SpO2 91 percent on 2 L nasal cannula. What is the most appropriate next step in his screening?

Confounding: A 42-year-old woman who is a case in a matched case-control study of venous thromboembolism is seen in a women's health clinic. Investigators report a crude odds ratio of 3.1 for combined oral contraceptive use. Her research record shows she smokes one pack per day, and smoking is more common among cases than controls. Blood pressure is 128/80 mm Hg and BMI is 27 kg/m2. The study team wants a valid estimate of the contraceptive effect. Which of the following is the best next step?

Counselling: A 70-year-old man visits his primary care clinic after reading about a case-control study linking a common medication to bladder cancer. The report gives an odds ratio of 4.0. He has taken the medication for three years, has no hematuria, and asks whether his chance of developing bladder cancer is four times that of a non-user. Vital signs and examination are normal, and urinalysis is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most accurate counselling response?

Outbreak investigation: A 6-year-old boy is admitted to a pediatric hospital in rural Iowa with bloody diarrhea, pallor, and oliguria. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, platelets 42,000/mm3, and creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, consistent with hemolytic uremic syndrome. Stool culture grows Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli O157:H7. Over the next week, the county health department identifies three more children with the same syndrome, none of whom share a household contact. Which of the following is the best next step in the investigation?

Recall bias: A 57-year-old woman with newly diagnosed hepatocellular carcinoma is enrolled by a research nurse in a hospital-based case-control study of prior medication exposures. Cases and age-matched controls are interviewed about medications taken over the previous 10 years. She is uncertain of some drug names and reports an over-the-counter supplement during a period she cannot date. Examination shows jaundice and a palpable liver edge. Which of the following is the best next step to reduce recall bias in this study?

Selection bias: A 66-year-old woman with a hip fracture is enrolled in a hospital-based case-control study of long-term sedative use and fracture risk. Controls are other women admitted to the orthopedic ward for elective knee replacement, a group with high sedative use. Her bone density is low, vital signs are stable, and she reports no falls at home. The study finds no association, which conflicts with earlier community data. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 52-year-old man is enrolled in a multicenter trial of a long-acting local anesthetic injected at two sites for knee surgery. A research nurse's frequency table shows one recorded block duration of 135 minutes, while most durations fall between 480 and 600 minutes. His chart documents an uneventful surgery and controlled pain. Vitals are 122/76 mm Hg and pulse 70/min. The investigator must decide how to handle this value before analysis. Which is the best next step?

A 41-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes comes to her primary care clinic to review a new oral medication. She read a trial summary reporting that the drug lowered HbA1c by an average of 1.0 percentage point, expressed as a mean with a standard error of the mean. She is worried the average hides large differences between patients. Her blood pressure is 128/78 mm Hg, BMI 31 kg/m2. Which of the following is the best next step in answering her concern?

A 52-year-old man with hypertension enrolls in a trial of a new antihypertensive agent at an academic clinic. After 12 weeks, the mean systolic pressure has fallen by 14 mm Hg. The manuscript reports the mean with the standard error of the mean, and a journal reviewer asks the authors to describe how much individual patients' blood pressure responses varied around that average. Which revision is most appropriate?

A 52-year-old woman who manages a primary care clinic's hypertension audit counts the follow-up visits each of ten patients required last quarter: 4, 5, 5, 5, 7, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10. The audit includes every patient the practice treated for hypertension during that quarter, so these ten patients are the entire population of interest. Which standard deviation should she report?

A 63-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer meets his oncologist to discuss a new chemotherapy regimen. The oncologist reads him a trial summary reporting a mean life expectancy gain of 5 years compared with standard therapy, and he asks how much benefit he can personally expect. The summary provides no other statistics. Before counseling him, which additional information is most important to review?

A 61-year-old man is admitted for elective total hip replacement, and the hospital quality team is reviewing length of stay for 200 recent surgical patients. Most stays fall between 2 and 5 days, with a median of 3 days, but a few patients with deep wound infections stayed more than 30 days. The distribution has a long right tail and the team must summarize a typical stay for an executive report. Which summary measure is most appropriate?

A 34-year-old man visits a clinic to review a laboratory result for a biomarker that a reference laboratory compares with a healthy population. His value lies more than 3 standard deviations above the healthy mean. He has no symptoms, his examination is normal, and the specimen was sent to a different laboratory than usual. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 34-year-old woman presents to a community health clinic for routine screening. She has no complaints, takes no medications, and her physical examination is normal. Her serum ferritin is 48 ng/mL. The clinic laboratory is establishing a reference range from its database of 500 healthy adult women, whose values form an approximately normal bell-shaped distribution with a mean of 48 ng/mL and a standard deviation of 20 ng/mL. Which range should the laboratory report as the reference interval?

A 40-year-old woman with fatigue and palpitations comes to an outpatient clinic. Her serum magnesium result is reported as a z score of +3.4 relative to a healthy reference sample, and the laboratory flags it as an extreme value. Her heart rate is 104/min, blood pressure 118/74 mm Hg, and she takes an over-the-counter supplement. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 45-year-old man is one of 10 workers at a small plant in an occupational health census, in which every worker's hemoglobin is measured and the health officer wants to describe how spread out the values are among these workers. The officer's spreadsheet lists all 10 values, and the team plans to report one measure of scatter for this group alone. Which calculation of the standard deviation is appropriate?

A 64-year-old man is admitted to a cardiac step-down unit for heart failure. A quality team reviews 60 recent admissions and reports a mean length of stay of 9 days with a standard deviation of 14 days. Most stays were 3 to 5 days, but three patients stayed more than 60 days after complications. His blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg. The discharge planning team asks how these data should be summarized. Which of the following is the best approach?

A 67-year-old man admitted with pneumonia is one of 300 patients in a hospital quality review of door-to-antibiotic times. Most times cluster between 40 and 60 minutes, but one entry reads 135 minutes, and a z-score check flags four values beyond three standard deviations from the mean. The analyst plans to delete all flagged values before reporting results to hospital leadership. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 44-year-old man with gout presents to the rheumatology clinic after his third acute flare in a year. Each flare began within 48 hours of a heavy evening of beer and red meat, with no other identifiable trigger. He takes allopurinol 300 mg daily, his serum urate is 6.8 mg/dL, and his BMI is 31 kg/m2. He asks whether alcohol is truly the trigger for his flares. Which study design would best evaluate this transient, individual-level trigger?

A 56-year-old woman with a family history of colorectal cancer is seen in a preventive medicine clinic after reading a local study. A case-control study of 120 patients with a rare cancer and 120 matched controls found that prior daily use of a specific herbal supplement was more frequent in cases, with an odds ratio of 3.1. She takes the supplement daily and asks whether this proves it causes cancer. Her examination and vital signs are normal. What is the most appropriate response?

A 57-year-old man with obesity presents to his primary care clinic for a routine visit. He has read a survey report finding that people who use a certain nightly sleep aid have higher rates of hypertension, and he asks whether he should stop his own medication. He takes no antihypertensive drugs. His blood pressure today is 146/92 mm Hg on repeat measurement, and his examination is otherwise unremarkable. The survey was a single-time snapshot. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 34-year-old woman presents to an urgent care clinic in a rural county with fever, cramps, and watery diarrhea that began two days after a community potluck. Her temperature is 38.6 C, heart rate 104/min, and blood pressure 118/74 mm Hg. Stool testing is pending, and several other attendees have similar symptoms. The county health team plans a case-control investigation to identify the implicated food. Which control group should the team select?

A 55-year-old woman with obesity presents to her primary care clinic to discuss weight management. A county health report shows that counties with more fast-food restaurants have higher average diabetes prevalence, and she asks whether this means she will develop diabetes. Her BMI is 34 kg/m2, fasting glucose is 110 mg/dL, and HbA1c is 6.1 percent. She is physically inactive and her mother has type 2 diabetes. What is the most appropriate next step in counseling her?

A 52-year-old man with type 2 diabetes presents to his primary care clinic with questions about an online study he read. Investigators enrolled adults who did or did not take a medication, followed each group prospectively for 10 years, and recorded who developed the outcome. He is otherwise healthy, his blood pressure is 128/80 mm Hg, and his HbA1c is 7.2 percent. He wants to understand what the study's main measure of effect means for his own risk. Which measure of effect should the physician use to interpret this study?

A 63-year-old man with Parkinson disease presents to a neurology clinic for follow-up. Years after diagnosis, he joined a case-control study and was asked to describe past pesticide exposures on farms decades earlier. He has a resting tremor, mild bradykinesia, and a normal mini-mental state examination. The study reports a stronger link between pesticides and Parkinson disease than earlier cohort data. Which type of bias is most likely to have inflated this association?

A 45-year-old woman with obesity and prediabetes presents to a community clinic for counseling. A county health report shows that counties with more fast-food outlets have higher diabetes prevalence, and she asks whether her own fast-food visits explain her risk. She reports four visits weekly, has a BMI of 33 kg/m2, and her repeat fasting glucose is 108 mg/dL. She has no other individual dietary data. What is the most appropriate next step in her counseling?

A 41-year-old man presents to an infectious disease clinic with three violaceous plaques on his lower legs that have enlarged over 2 months. He reports sex with men and no recent travel. His vital signs are normal, and cervical lymph nodes are palpable. Biopsy confirms Kaposi sarcoma. A case-control study at the clinic found HIV infection much more common among patients with this lesion than among matched controls. The team wants stronger evidence that HIV causes the tumor. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 31-year-old man presents to a county emergency department with 3 days of bloody diarrhea, fever of 38.9 C, and crampy abdominal pain. Stool culture grows Salmonella, and he is one of 40 similar cases reported this week after a catered picnic. Vital signs show heart rate 98/min and blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg, with mild dehydration. Public health officials want to identify the food responsible. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 29-year-old woman with frequent migraine attacks presents to a neurology clinic in an outpatient setting. She reports that attacks begin within hours of drinking red wine, but only on some occasions, and she wants to know whether alcohol truly triggers her individual episodes. She is otherwise healthy, takes no daily medications, and her neurologic examination is normal. Her two-year headache diary records dates of attacks and all alcohol intake. Which study approach would best test whether alcohol triggers her own attacks?

A 64-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and a prior hospitalization for exacerbation presents to his pulmonologist in a regional health system. A county-level report shows that counties with higher average particulate air pollution have higher rates of emergency visits for respiratory illness. The patient asks whether his own exposure explains his recent visits. He lives in a low-pollution suburb, his spirometry shows a stable FEV1, and his vital signs are normal. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 63-year-old man with hypertension presents to a primary care clinic for follow-up. He has read a large prospective cohort study that followed adults taking a daily antiplatelet drug and adults not taking it, tracking who developed stroke over ten years. He asks how the investigators expressed the strength of the drug's effect on stroke risk. His blood pressure today is 136/84 mm Hg and his examination is unremarkable. Which measure of effect should the study have reported?

A 68-year-old man in the intensive care unit has had a central venous catheter for 12 days. He received fluconazole prophylaxis earlier this admission. He has fever to 38.9 C and hypotension requiring norepinephrine. He is alert with no focal neurologic deficits, and the insertion site is clean. Two blood culture sets, one drawn from the catheter and one peripherally, both grow Candida glabrata. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 66-year-old woman is seen in clinic 2 weeks after total knee replacement at a US community hospital. She has fever to 38.4 C, a draining wound with erythema, blood pressure 124/76 mm Hg, and heart rate 98/min. Wound culture grows methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Hospital review finds a lapse in the operating room wound-care protocol. She asks whether the infection was preventable and why it happened. Which of the following is the best approach to communicating this healthcare-associated infection?

A 72-year-old man on a medical ward received ceftriaxone for pneumonia and now has watery diarrhea for 3 days. He has about 6 unformed stools daily, temperature 37.4 C, and mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without peritoneal signs. His pneumonia has resolved and he is clinically improved. WBC is 13,000/mm3 and creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, with no hypotension or ileus. Stool toxin assay is positive for Clostridioides difficile. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 67-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes is hospitalized on a medical ward for pyelonephritis. She speaks limited English, and her adult son has interpreted at every visit. Hospital review finds that a central venous catheter placed on day 3 was the likely source of a Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection, with an incomplete insertion checklist. She is now afebrile, temperature 37.1 C, blood pressure 128/76 mm Hg, and she asks her team what happened. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 71-year-old woman on a medical ward has had an indwelling urinary catheter for 12 days after hip fracture repair. She has dementia, which is her baseline. She has no fever, flank pain, suprapubic tenderness, or new urinary symptoms. Temperature is 36.9 C, blood pressure 128/74 mm Hg, and heart rate 80/min. Urinalysis is positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite. Urine culture grows more than 100,000 CFU/mL of Escherichia coli. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 58-year-old man in the medical intensive care unit has a non-tunneled right internal jugular central venous catheter placed 6 days ago. He has had fever to 39.2 C, chills, and hypotension that responded to fluids. Examination shows a clean, nontender insertion site without erythema or purulence. Peripheral and catheter-drawn blood cultures were obtained, and the catheter-drawn set grew gram-positive cocci in clusters within 14 hours. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

An 81-year-old woman with dementia on a medical ward has had an indwelling urinary catheter for 14 days for urinary retention. She has temperature 38.4 C, new confusion, and suprapubic tenderness. Blood pressure is 118/70 mm Hg with no hypotension. Urinalysis shows pyuria and positive nitrite. Catheter urine culture grows more than 100,000 CFU/mL of Escherichia coli. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 68-year-old man with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is seen in the cardiology clinic. Six weeks ago an outside clinician started sildenafil for pulmonary hypertension estimated on echocardiography. He now has orthopnea, bibasilar crackles, and oxygen saturation of 91 percent on room air. Blood pressure is 148/88 mm Hg. Echocardiography shows a dilated left atrium and preserved ejection fraction. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 52-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis presents to the cardiology clinic in the United States with 3 weeks of palpitations and exertional breathlessness. Pulse is irregularly irregular at 104/min and blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg. Examination reveals a loud opening snap and a low-pitched diastolic rumble. Echocardiography shows severe mitral stenosis with left atrial enlargement, and the electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation. She has no prior stroke and her kidney function is normal. What is the most appropriate anticoagulant for stroke prevention?

A 68-year-old man with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and long-standing hypertension presents to the cardiology clinic in the United States with progressive exertional dyspnea and ankle swelling. He has atrial fibrillation and a body mass index of 34. Blood pressure is 150/88 mmHg, weight is up 3 kg over 2 weeks, and bilateral crackles are present. Echocardiography shows left atrial enlargement and diastolic dysfunction. Right heart catheterization shows an elevated pulmonary artery wedge pressure with a pulmonary vascular resistance that is not elevated. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 17-year-old man with prior acute rheumatic fever with carditis at age 9 presents to a primary care clinic in the United States for routine follow-up. He has mild exertional fatigue, no fever, and has received no antibiotic prophylaxis since leaving pediatric care a year ago. The pharynx is clear. Examination shows a grade 2 apical holosystolic murmur. Heart rate is 76/min and blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg. Echocardiography shows chronic mitral regurgitation without active inflammation. What is the most appropriate next step to prevent recurrent rheumatic fever?

A 34-year-old woman with known rheumatic mitral and aortic valve disease presents to the emergency department in the United States with 5 days of fever, chills and fatigue. Temperature is 38.9 C, pulse 112/min, and blood pressure 96/60 mmHg. Examination reveals a new diastolic murmur at the aortic area that was not documented previously. The chest is clear. Laboratory studies show leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 34-year-old woman with known rheumatic mitral valve disease is seen in the clinic. For five days she has had fever to 38.6 C, fatigue, and night sweats. She reports a dental extraction two weeks ago. Examination shows a new regurgitant murmur and splinter hemorrhages on the fingers. Her heart rate is 104/min and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 52-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with three days of palpitations and worsening exertional breathlessness. She has a known history of rheumatic heart disease, and she has been told she has mitral stenosis. She has no focal neurologic deficit and her blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg with an irregularly irregular pulse of 102/min. Transthoracic echocardiography shows severe mitral stenosis with a left atrial appendage filling defect consistent with thrombus. Which of the following is the most appropriate anticoagulant for her?

An 11-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic with three weeks of fever, migratory pain in the knees and ankles, and fatigue. Three weeks earlier he had a sore throat treated at home. Examination shows a new apical systolic murmur, erythema marginatum on the trunk, and small subcutaneous nodules. Heart rate is 112/min, temperature 38.4 C. Which of the following best explains the mechanism of his carditis?

A 10-year-old girl presents to the pediatric clinic in the United States with 3 weeks of fever and migrating pain in the knees and ankles. She had a sore throat about 3 weeks ago that resolved without treatment. Temperature is 38.4 C and pulse is 110/min. The knees and ankles are warm and swollen with limited movement, and a soft holosystolic murmur is heard at the apex. No skin nodules are present. Antistreptolysin O titer is elevated. What is the most likely mechanism underlying this presentation?

A 63-year-old woman, a physician researcher at a community clinic, compares two oral analgesics in 40 patients with knee osteoarthritis. After one week, pain relief is coded as none, mild, moderate, or complete, and the distributions are skewed and uneven between groups. Her colleague proposes an independent-samples t-test on the numeric codes. Which analysis is the most appropriate next step?

A 61-year-old woman, a family physician at a community health center, reviews systolic blood pressure readings from 1,200 patients in her panel for the clinic board. The distribution is strongly right skewed, with a small group of readings above 240 mm Hg from patients who had missed their medications. She must choose one summary value to represent the typical patient. Which summary should she report?

A 64-year-old man with hypertension attends a county clinic where his blood pressure is 148/92 mm Hg on a single reading. A health department analyst reports blood pressure control rates of 58 percent at clinic A and 66 percent at clinic B. Clinic A serves a much older population, and the analyst plans to rank the clinics using these crude figures. Which next step best supports a fair comparison of clinic performance?

A 49-year-old man with a 30-pack-year smoking history is seen at a county health department for an annual wellness visit. His examination is unremarkable and his blood pressure is 128/80 mm Hg. A surveillance report notes 40 new lung cancer diagnoses among 2,000 county residents who were free of lung cancer at baseline, observed over one year. The health department must describe this one-year risk. Which measure best describes it?

A 46-year-old woman, a nurse practitioner at a rural community health center, compiles a screening registry of 800 adults. For each patient she records blood type (A, B, AB, or O) and fasting glucose in mg/dL. She plans an annual report grouping patients by blood type, and her colleague notes that the blood type categories have no inherent order. Which measurement scale best describes blood type?

A 38-year-old woman presents to a community health center for a routine visit. Her electronic record captures her ABO blood group, a self-rated pain score from 0 to 10, her body temperature in degrees Celsius, and the number of cigarettes she smokes daily. Vitals are normal and she reports no acute symptoms. The clinic is building a dataset for population analysis. Which recorded variable has a true zero, so ratio comparisons between patients are valid?

A 49-year-old man, a community health worker at a county clinic, records body mass index to one decimal place for 500 adults screened at a health fair. Values range from 17 to 52. He must present the distribution of this continuous variable to the county health board, which needs to see how values cluster. Which graph is most appropriate for displaying this distribution?

A 58-year-old woman, quality manager of a diabetes clinic in a suburban health system, has hemoglobin A1c results for 120 patients measured at each of the last 12 quarterly visits. She wants to show whether the clinic's average A1c has been falling across the year. Her staff drafted a pie chart, a box plot of pooled values, and a histogram of pooled values. Which graph best shows the change in average A1c over time?

A 57-year-old man with type 2 diabetes is seen in a primary care clinic while the clinic prepares a lipid audit. His blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg and his fasting triglyceride level is 310 mg/dL. Among 40 audited patients, most values cluster between 100 and 250 mg/dL, but a few exceed 1000 mg/dL, creating a long right tail. The quality team must summarize and display these values in its report. Which summary and display best describes this distribution?

A 3-year-old boy is seen in neurology clinic in an outpatient setting for progressive spasticity of both legs and poor growth over two years. He had episodes of irritability and vomiting during infections. He has a stiff gait, hyperreflexia, and no seizures. Plasma ammonia is mildly elevated at 75 micromol/L on repeat testing, plasma arginine is markedly raised at 620 micromol/L, and plasma citrulline is low-normal. He is on a protein-restricted diet, and weight is at the 5th percentile. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 5-day-old girl is transferred to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit with seizures and a bulging fontanelle. Protein intake has been stopped, and she has received intravenous glucose, lipid, sodium benzoate, and arginine for six hours. Her plasma ammonia remains markedly elevated and is still rising. Neuroimaging shows cerebral edema. Heart rate is 172/min, blood pressure 68/40 mm Hg, and temperature 36.9 C. Which intervention is most appropriate now?

A 7-year-old boy with arginase deficiency is seen in clinic for progressive spastic diplegia and irritability. Arginine supplements were started at diagnosis, and he has otherwise been managed with protein restriction. His weight is below the 10th percentile. Plasma ammonia is 90 micromol/L and plasma arginine is markedly raised. Current medications are sodium phenylbutyrate and a multivitamin. Which change to his treatment is most appropriate?

A 31-year-old woman is seen in the genetics clinic after her 3-week-old son is diagnosed with ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency. She has no history of encephalopathy, protein intolerance, or episodes of vomiting. Her examination is normal, and her plasma ammonia is within normal limits on a fasting sample. The familial variant has been identified on molecular testing in her son. She asks whether she needs testing and whether her daughters are at risk. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 3-day-old boy is brought to the emergency department with two days of poor feeding, vomiting, and increasing lethargy after an uneventful term birth. He is drowsy with hypotonia, respiratory rate 58/min, heart rate 164/min, and temperature 36.8 C. Plasma ammonia is markedly elevated. Arterial blood gas shows respiratory alkalosis with a normal anion gap, and plasma glucose is normal. Blood cultures have been drawn. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 4-day-old boy is brought to the emergency department from home after 2 days of poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy and fast breathing. He was born at term after an uneventful delivery and fed well initially. Temperature is 37.1 C, heart rate 168/min, respiratory rate 70/min, and he is drowsy and hypotonic. Plasma ammonia is 480 micromol/L, arterial pH 7.52 with PaCO2 25 mmHg, and anion gap 11. Blood cultures are pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate next step in management?

A 19-year-old woman with known partial ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is in the intensive care unit after an emergency appendectomy. Over the past 12 hours she has received intravenous glucose, lipids, insulin, sodium benzoate and arginine. She is now drowsy with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 8. Temperature is 37.4 C, heart rate 110/min and blood pressure 130/80 mmHg. Plasma ammonia has risen to 620 micromol/L despite therapy. Brain imaging shows cerebral oedema. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 2-day-old boy born at term in a community hospital presents with poor feeding, lethargy, vomiting and tachypnoea. He fed well for the first 24 hours. Heart rate is 168/min, respiratory rate 66/min and temperature 36.9 C. He is drowsy with intermittent jerking movements. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.52, pCO2 22 mmHg and bicarbonate 20 mmol/L. Plasma ammonia is 480 micromol/L and blood glucose 5.1 mmol/L. Blood cultures are pending. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 31-year-old woman with known partial ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is seen in neurology clinic in an outpatient setting after a generalized seizure. She has had two episodes of confusion in the past year during influenza-like illnesses, managed on a protein-restricted diet with sodium phenylbutyrate. Vital signs are normal and neurological examination is nonfocal. Plasma ammonia is 95 micromol/L, and her anticonvulsant is being selected. She is otherwise well, weighs 58 kg, and her growth has been stable. Which of the following is the most appropriate antiseizure medication to start?

A 2-day-old girl is evaluated in the newborn nursery at a community hospital after feeding poorly and becoming lethargic since birth. She was born at 39 weeks after an unremarkable delivery. Heart rate is 150/min, respiratory rate 64/min with grunting, temperature 36.9 C, and she is hypotonic with intermittent posturing. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.48, PaCO2 22 mmHg, and bicarbonate 19 mmol/L. Anion gap is 12 mmol/L, and plasma ammonia is 350 micromol/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman is evaluated in the emergency department after three days of vomiting, confusion, and drowsiness that began during a viral illness. She has avoided high-protein foods for years and reports two similar episodes in adolescence. Temperature is 37.0 C, heart rate 96/min, and blood pressure 112/70 mm Hg. She is oriented to person only and has asterixis. Plasma ammonia is elevated and urine orotic acid is markedly increased. Plasma citrulline is low. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?

A 31-year-old woman in the postpartum period is admitted to the medical ward with confusion after two days of vomiting. She has a history of episodic protein aversion and drowsiness during a prior viral illness. Her younger brother died in infancy. Temperature is 37.2 C, pulse 98/min and blood pressure 118/74 mmHg. She is disoriented to time. Plasma ammonia is 210 micromol/L, arterial pH 7.49, pCO2 24 mmHg and anion gap 11 mmol/L. Which test is most useful to localise the enzymatic block?

A 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 12 years presents to his primary care clinic for annual screening. He has no edema, foamy urine, or symptoms. Blood pressure is 128/78 mm Hg and BMI is 31. Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL with eGFR 78 mL/min/1.73 m2. A spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio is 85 mg/g, and urinalysis shows no hematuria. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 68-year-old man presents to his primary care clinic for an annual visit. He has no cough, weight loss, or hemoptysis and feels well. He smoked one pack per day for 45 years and quit 4 years ago. Vital signs are normal, and lung and cardiac examinations are unremarkable. He asks whether he should be screened for lung cancer. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 61-year-old man who is a former smoker presents to his primary care clinic for follow-up after treatment of stage I lung cancer found on low-dose CT screening. Vital signs and examination are normal. Clinic data show 5-year survival for lung cancer has risen since screening began, yet county lung cancer death rates are unchanged. Which best explains the apparent survival improvement?

A 49-year-old woman with no risk factors attends a community health fair in a low-prevalence area. She has no symptoms, and her rapid anti-hepatitis C antibody test is reactive. Liver enzymes obtained at the fair are normal, and vital signs are unremarkable. She has no history of injection drug use or transfusion. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, presents to her obstetric clinic at 30 weeks of gestation for routine prenatal care. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and she has no drug allergies. She received the influenza vaccine last fall but has had no Tdap during this pregnancy. Vital signs are normal, and fundal height matches dates. Which vaccine is most appropriate to administer at this visit?

A 32-year-old woman presents to her primary care clinic for a routine preventive visit. She has no history of injection drug use, tattoos, blood transfusion, or known blood exposure, and she is not pregnant. Vital signs are normal, and her liver examination is unremarkable. Her ALT and AST are normal, and her platelet count is 240,000/mm3. Universal one-time screening reveals a reactive hepatitis C antibody test. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 34-year-old woman who works as a county epidemiologist is notified of 14 cases of vomiting and diarrhea among attendees of a church supper held on Saturday evening. Symptom onset in every case fell within a 6-hour window, and no new cases have appeared 48 hours later. Stool testing is positive for norovirus in several patients. Which is the most appropriate next step in the investigation?

A 58-year-old man with COPD presents to the emergency department with 4 days of fever, dry cough, and watery diarrhea. Five days ago he returned from a business trip, and two other hotel guests were hospitalized with pneumonia. Temperature is 40.1 C, heart rate 112/min, blood pressure 108/66 mm Hg, and SpO2 90% on room air. Examination reveals right basilar crackles. Chest radiograph shows right lower lobe consolidation, and serum sodium is 126 mEq/L. Which test is most appropriate next?

A 29-year-old man presents to the emergency department with 3 days of jaundice, nausea, and right upper quadrant pain. He ate at a restaurant 10 days ago, and two other diners who ate there that evening developed similar illness. Temperature is 37.9 C, with scleral icterus and mild hepatomegaly. AST is 1,450 U/L, ALT is 1,820 U/L, and IgM anti-hepatitis A antibody is positive. Which is the most appropriate next step in the public health response?

A 61-year-old man with obesity presents to an outpatient clinic for follow-up. He is a retired accountant with no symptoms of diabetes. Height and weight give a BMI of 33. Blood pressure is 134/84 mm Hg. Two HbA1c tests, drawn three months apart, were both in the prediabetes range. He is sedentary and eats large portions of fast food. He asks how to prevent diabetes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 69-year-old man presents to a primary care clinic for a routine follow-up. He is retired and has no symptoms of diabetes. At age 66, his fasting plasma glucose was in the normal range during a preventive visit, and he has not been tested since. Height and weight give a BMI of 27. Blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. He walks regularly and has no family history of diabetes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 61-year-old man presents to a primary care clinic for routine preventive care. He has no symptoms of diabetes and no prior diabetes diagnosis. His BMI is 27.4, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. Today's fasting plasma glucose is normal, and his last screening three years ago was also normal. His family history is negative, and examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate interval for his next screening?

A 37-year-old Asian American woman presents to a primary care clinic for a routine wellness visit. She has no symptoms of diabetes, has never had glucose testing, and has no family history of diabetes. She walks several times weekly and does not smoke. Height is 160 cm and weight is 60 kg, giving a BMI of 23.4. Blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg, and examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 35-year-old man presents to a primary care clinic for an annual preventive visit. He is a software engineer with no symptoms of diabetes, including no polyuria, polydipsia, or blurred vision. He takes no medications. Height is 1.78 m and weight is 98 kg, giving a BMI of 31. Blood pressure is 128/82 mm Hg. His father has type 2 diabetes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 46-year-old Asian American woman presents to a primary care clinic for a routine preventive visit. She has no symptoms of diabetes, such as polyuria, polydipsia, or unexplained weight loss. Her sister has type 2 diabetes. Height is 1.60 m and weight is 61 kg, giving a BMI of 24. Blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg. She walks daily and eats a balanced diet. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 41-year-old woman with a traumatic spinal cord injury has had an intrathecal baclofen pump for 3 years. She arrives at the emergency department with 2 days of fever to 39.4 C, agitation, and severe generalized rigidity with painful spasms. Her pump refill was due 9 days ago and was missed. Heart rate is 128/min and blood pressure 176/98 mmHg. Creatine kinase is 9,400 U/L with leukocytosis. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 74-year-old woman with obstructive sleep apnea is on the surgical ward 6 hours after a hip replacement. She uses a morphine patient-controlled analgesia pump with a background infusion and received several overnight doses. She is difficult to rouse, and her respiratory rate is 7 breaths per minute with pinpoint pupils. SpO2 is 86% on room air and blood pressure is 102/60 mmHg. Pain cannot be assessed. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
